author: lax leader
title: Teoscar Hernández expected to begin rehab assignment next week for Dodgers
text:
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Teoscar Hernández could start his rehab assignment as soon as next week as he works to return from a hamstring injury, according to a June 17 update.
Hernández injured his left hamstring on May 27 while sprinting to first base against the Colorado Rockies. He sustained a Grade 1 hamstring strain, which typically keeps players out for about a month. In response, the Dodgers called up Ryan Ward to fill in during Hernández’s absence.
Hernández has been making progress in his recovery and was seen working out at Dodger Stadium on Sunday. Manager Dave Roberts said that Hernández will participate in a simulated game on Thursday, an off day for the team, and is expected to begin his rehab assignment early next week, Fredo Cervantes of the Sporting Tribune reported. Katie Woo of The Athletic indicated that the rehab stint could start as soon as Tuesday in Reno, Nevada, where Triple-A Oklahoma City Comets are scheduled to play.
The Dodgers are currently dealing with several injuries across their roster. Starting pitchers Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow have missed significant time due to injuries. World Series hero Will Smith is also sidelined, along with Kike Hernández who re-injured himself after returning from offseason surgery.
Some players such as Mookie Betts and Tommy Edman have returned from injury recently, but getting Teoscar Hernández back remains important for the team’s lineup depth. Aaron Coloma of Dodgers Nation wrote that although Hernández started slowly this season, he had begun improving before being sidelined: “He has a .784 OPS over the course of the season, hitting seven homers and driving in 31 RBIs,” Coloma wrote. “Over the past couple of weeks, though, he has been one of the Dodgers’ biggest offensive threats.”
Coloma added: “He has a 195 wRC+ during that time, hitting three homers with 14 RBIs. He’s slashing .375/.426/.625 in that period, which gives him a better OPS than all of his teammates except Shohei Ohtani during that stretch.”
